change: Precompute output and input row pointers outside the matrix inner loop, exposing the column-only memory index to the existing vectorizer. No reassociation or fused multiply-add change.
validation: 289 checks passed in 12.15s using the independent C-bootstrap compiler; native/web default/release, float32/float64 products, native one/two threads and explicit SSE2 fallback. Earlier focused run: 285 passed in 9.36s.
initial_result: 192x192, eight products: about 96ms single-thread default/release against 22ms C, identifying missing vectorization. See before.json for all samples; do not compare these absolute times against later runs.
method: Seven alternating paired samples per shape, CPUs 2/3, one/two Dewy threads. C always one thread, -O3 -march=native -ffp-contract=off. Initialization/worker startup excluded; allocations, zeroing, and replacing prior output included. Independent integer checksum oracle for 0/1/17/65, C checksum for full workload; regression test checks every output against a closed-form reference on a 65x64 by 64x67 product.
ir_evidence: The extracted matrix callback has no vector memory operations before; after it contains AVX2 and SSE2 vector load, multiply, add and store loops, plus scalar tail.
limits: This measures the bundled numeric matrix operator, not all user loops or tuned BLAS. Default remains materially slower than C.
Large-case baseline two-thread release had substantial host noise; retain all samples, prioritize paired single-thread comparisons for language costs.
A comment explaining the invariant pointers was added after compiler builds; executable code is unchanged.

Initial benchmark fixtures needed parenthesized Dewy casts and the missing C dimension argument; fixed before measurements. A Python fixture-registration line was initially inserted inside a Dewy test string; moved before successful validation.
